[Feature][MoE] Fuse the shared expert into the A5 MegaMoe operator for W4A4 MXFP4 (enable_fused_mc2=3) (#18053)

## What

Fuse the shared expert into the A5 CANN MegaMoe operator
(`enable_fused_mc2=3`), extending #17654 with W4A4 MXFP4 support and
fixing activation-enum handling.

## Why

With `enable_fused_mc2=2`, the shared expert runs as a separate
GMM1+activation+GMM2 forward alongside the MegaMoe routed path.
`enable_fused_mc2=3` folds the shared expert into the MegaMoe kernel so
its weights travel with the routed weights and the extra kernels
disappear. #17654 implemented this for W8A8 MXFP checkpoints only; W4A4
MXFP4 models (e.g. GLM-5.3-W4A4C8-MXFP4) silently fell back to the
separate shared-expert forward.

Three additional gaps found while enabling it for W4A4:

1. The routed-activation guard compared the `MoEActivation` enum via
`str(...)`, which renders as `MoEActivation.SILU` and never matches
`"silu"`, so fusion was disabled even for standard SiLU models. Because
the operator applies a single global activation to the shared experts,
the guard was then generalized to a "same activation function" check:
equal activation type plus equal activation params (see How).
2. Packed-FP4 shared weights need the same layout rebuild as the routed
experts: `w1` cast to `FRACTAL_NZ`, `w2` rebuilt as `FRACTAL_NZ_C0_32`
on an fp8 carrier from the packed fp4 buffer, and the byte-stored E8M0
scales viewed as `float8_e8m0fnu`.
3. An unbounded shared `SiluAndMul` was unconditionally accepted even
when the routed swiglu carries a `swiglu_limit` clamp, which would
silently change shared-expert numerics under fusion.

## How

- `shared_experts.py`: accept `QuantType.W4A4MXFP` in the fusion gate;
in the weight collector, branch on the quant type to apply the
packed-FP4 FRACTAL_NZ / FRACTAL_NZ_C0_32 rebuild and E8M0 scale views,
mirroring the routed-expert weight processing in the W4A4 MoE method;
also check `mxfp4_tp_padding` alongside `mxfp8_tp_padding`; replace the
activation guard with a general equality check on (activation type,
activation_params) between the routed activation bound into the MegaMoe
call (mirroring `select_mega_moe_activation_kwargs`) and the shared
expert's activation module. Parameterized activations
(situglu/swigluoai) now fuse when their params match exactly;
same-class-different-params pairings, GELU/swiglustep-style activations
the operator cannot express, and an unbounded shared SiluAndMul under a
clamped routed swiglu all keep the separate shared-expert forward.
- `moe_comm_method.py`: keep passing
`**layer.mega_moe_activation_kwargs` alongside the new shared-expert
kwargs (conflict resolution against #17916).
- `additional_config.md`: document `enable_fused_mc2=3`.

## Test

- GLM-5.3-W4A4C8-MXFP4 on 8 x Ascend950DT, TP=8 + EP,
`enable_fused_mc2=3`, MTP speculative decoding: service starts, no
"keeping the separate shared-expert forward" fallback log, and `curl`
chat completions respond correctly with zero errors.

[Feature][Model] Integrate Kimi K3.1 on main (#20878)

**Targeted A3/A5 Triton operator validation is recorded below.
Full-model and multi-card behavior remain outside this follow-up's
validation.**


## What this PR does / why we need it



Ports the Kimi K3.1 changes from the v0.30.0 development line to the
current main baseline. The changes cover model and runner integration,
KDA/PCP, sparse attention and QLI, DCP communication, paired KV-cache
allocation, Mooncake transfers, attention residual operators and
quantized paths.


This is the integration PR. Twelve review-only slices were prepared by
responsibility, with shared files split by change block. Their
fixed-base reconstruction was verified at regrouping as recorded below.
Subsequent integration amendments, including the 2026-11-09 review
cleanup, are tracked here; the slices remain focused review snapshots
and are not intended to merge independently.


The mainline removal of legacy TP-based DSA-CP is retained. The private
branch's legacy-specific local query-length/leading-zero behavior is not
carried over; equivalence with PCP has not been established. This is an
explicit scope limitation, not a claim that PCP is equivalent.


Follow-up on 2026-11-05: The PROLOG_V3 implementation is selected by the
existing `self.use_rope` execution flag: `False` binds
`cann_ops_transformer.mla_prolog` for NoPE while preserving the learned
tail dimension; `True` retains `torch_npu.npu_mla_prolog_v3`, including
RoPE-enabled K3.1. RoPE-enabled workers do not require the optional CANN
extension for this binding. No new configuration flag is introduced.


Follow-up on 2026-11-05: KDA state-copy now uses the shared Triton JIT
warmup registry. Bound cache layouts are late-registered before
`registry.warmup()`; startup uses compile-only tensor metadata, and
serving uses the same launcher. This removes temporary startup copies
and version-dependent manual compiled-launch argument lists. The A3
byte-copy fallback follows the same mechanism. These changes and the
RMSNorm gate changes are reviewed together in #20887 (Triton operator
updates).


## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?



Yes. It adds K3.1 execution paths and changes supported attention,
caching and distributed execution configurations.

[Feature][Performance][xlite] Update to xlite attention metadata V2 and remove padded tokens/requests from forward (#20938)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR migrates the `xlite` backend from attention metadata V1 (the
built backend metadata) to attention metadata V2, built directly from
the runner-retained `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata`, and removes padded
tokens/requests from the xlite forward. The `xlite` package needs to be
bumped to `0.2.0rc5` for the `AttnMetaV2` runtime / `forward_v2`
contract (dependency bump shipped in #20937).

Per forward call, the pre-V2 xlite wrapper had to:

1. route the *built* backend metadata (`AscendMetadata` /
`AscendMLAMetadata` / `AscendSFAMetadata`) to CPU via
`AttnMetadataRouter` (device→host copies),
2. call `.item()` on `(block_tables[:, 0] != 0).sum()` — a **blocking
D2H sync** every step,
3. `.tolist()` the lens/cached_lens and the whole block table into
Python lists, marshalled into C++ and copied H2D inside xlite's forward,
4. re-materialize `positions` (`.contiguous()` + reshape — an extra
copy),
5. cross streams with an explicit
`curr_stream.wait_stream(npu_update_stream)`.

With metadata V2, `XliteWrapper.__call__` builds `AttnMetaV2` straight
from the runner-retained `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` (the raw
pre-builder per-request state, group 0):

- `query_start_loc` / `positions` / `slot_mapping` / `block_tables` pass
through **as device views** of the runner's buffers — no slicing, no
copies. The persistent full-width block table and the over-long slot
mapping pass through as-is; xlite's C++ narrows the table width itself
(`SliceBlockTableToLens`, host-lists only, no device sync).
- Only `lens` / `cached_lens` are derived tensors (the only fields no
backend ships), computed **on device** (`diff(query_start_loc)` and
`clamp(seq_lens − lens, 0)`); host mirrors come from CPU tensors the
runner already maintains (no D2H). Both are rejection-corrected at
source on the V2 model runner.
- Passing buffers through without clones is safe: xlite brackets its
forward with stream events (`EventWaitCurrStream` before,
`EventRecordCurrStream` after), so both the metadata-producing ops and
the next step's in-place buffer rewrites are stream-ordered against the
forward's reads.
- Padded tokens/requests are removed from the xlite forward: the model
runner's common metadata is request-exact (`num_reqs` /
`num_actual_tokens` are the real counts), so no padding requests are
forwarded. The model-runner-V1 adaptations of the earlier revision
(padding-request front-walk, `_seq_lens_cpu` fallback, V1 return
contracts) are dropped entirely along with the upstream model-runner-V1
removal (#20097).
- Under DP, idle ranks run the engine dummy batch through the xlite
forward to keep the DP collectives aligned; a persistent one-token batch
metadata is allocated once (`XliteWrapper.dummy_batch()`) instead of
being rebuilt every idle step.
- `AttnMetadataRouter` (~150 lines) and the per-architecture
`_attn_metadata_type` runtime metadata-type checks are deleted — the
wrapper no longer depends on the built backend metadata types.
- The per-group common metadata stash in
`worker/v2/model_states/default.py` is now retained when xlite is
enabled (previously only for decoder replay), so the wrapper can reach
the group-0 common; a config without the xlite section counts as
disabled, keeping the shared worker path xlite-optional.
- Output contract: the wrapper returns exactly the padded input token
count of rows (`num_padded_input_tokens`) that consumers expect — e.g.
the speculator copies the target hidden states with
`self.hidden_states[:num_tokens_padded].copy_(hidden_states)`, which
requires the exact row count.

The migration requires `xlite >= 0.2.0rc5` (the `AttnMetaV2` runtime:
persistent block tables with C++-side width narrowing, `forward_v2`,
over-long slot-mapping/position extents).

lower per-step ITL in both xlite modes (numbers below). No API or

[BugFix] Restore has_sync_kv_loads bookkeeping in the copied schedulers (#20810)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Restores the `has_sync_kv_loads` bookkeeping that upstream vLLM's
`Scheduler.schedule()` performs, in the two vLLM-Ascend copies of that
method that had dropped it:

- `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py`
(`BalanceScheduler`)
- `vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py` (`DyntraLBScheduler`)

Without the flag, `SchedulerOutput.has_sync_kv_loads` keeps its default
`False` value. The worker derives `start_after_forward = not
scheduler_output.has_sync_kv_loads` from it, so `start_load_kv()` was
deferred until **after** the forward pass even when the current forward
needs KV cache that an external connector loads synchronously
(`load_kv_async=False`). With layerwise external KV loading the
per-layer `wait_for_layer_load()` then returns early, the model reads KV
cache that was never restored, and the output is corrupted.

Both copies now mirror upstream vLLM exactly:

- initialize `has_sync_kv_loads = False` per scheduling step;
- set it to `True` when a request is admitted with
`num_external_computed_tokens > 0` on the synchronous path (upstream's
comment `load_kv_async is False here` applies to the same branch);
- propagate it into `SchedulerOutput`.

`DyntraLBScheduler` keeps the file's existing
`_scheduler_output_supports(...)` guard, because it also supports vLLM
releases whose `SchedulerOutput` has no such field (`v0.26.0`).
`BalanceScheduler` targets the pinned vLLM release tag (`v0.32.0`),
which always carries the field, so it passes it directly — the same way
`vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py` and
`vllm_ascend/core/scheduler_profiling_chunk.py` already do.

Fixes #20725

The same omission exists on the `releases/v0.30.0` line, where the
reported
issue was reproduced. It is backported separately in #21454.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It fixes corrupted output when an external KV connector loads
synchronously while balance scheduling or dyntra load balancing is
enabled. A release note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added (CPU only, no NPU needed):
-
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py::test_balance_schedule_reports_sync_kv_loads`
-
`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py::test_balance_schedule_reports_sync_kv_loads_for_mixed_batch`
-
`tests/ut/core/test_dyntra_lb_scheduler.py::test_dyntra_lb_reports_sync_kv_loads`
-
`tests/ut/core/test_dyntra_lb_scheduler.py::test_dyntra_lb_reports_sync_kv_loads_for_mixed_batch`

The parametrized tests cover the three load shapes of the new
bookkeeping, for both schedulers:
- a synchronous external load (`load_kv_async=False`) must report
`has_sync_kv_loads=True`;
  - no external hit at all must keep it `False`;
- an asynchronous external load (`load_kv_async=True`) must keep it
`False`, because such a request stays in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and is
not admitted in that step.

The mixed-batch tests cover a single step that carries both a
synchronous and an asynchronous load: the flag is per-step, so the
synchronous load must still raise it.

  All of them fail without this fix.

- Static checks run locally: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`,
`tools/check_long_functions.py`, `tools/check_forbidden_imports.py`,
`tools/check_boolean_context_manager.py` — all pass.

- The unit tests themselves were **not** executed on the authoring
machine (no vLLM install available on that host); they are expected to

[BugFix] Preserve mixed-precision Kimi MLA output gates (#21387)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix a mixed-precision weight-loading regression exposed by the vLLM 0.33
Kimi MLA gate fusion.

Upstream AMD Kimi now packs `q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` and
`g_proj` into `KimiK3MergedQKVGateLinear`. Ascend's ModelSlim mapping
still describes only the first two shards. For quantized Q/KV with a
FLOAT gate, the fused layer therefore allocates INT8 storage for all

nongated draft projections and existing KDA mappings.

[Feature] Add int8 quantized all-reduce for large bf16 TP collectives on Atlas A2 (#19000)

## What does this PR do?

Adds an **opt-in int8 quantized all-reduce** for large bf16 TP
collectives on Atlas A2 (910B series), halving the communication volume
of the bandwidth-bound prefill all-reduces (o_proj / MoE combine).

## Motivation & context

On HCCS-interconnected Atlas A2 TP deployments, prefill-stage bf16
all-reduces dominate the non-overlapped communication time (~16% of
stage time for Qwen3.6-35B TP=4 with 16k-token batches; 81 all-reduces
per step, 64 MiB each at ~33 GB/s effective algorithm bandwidth).

### Scheme

1. **Per-channel symmetric scale with a world-size headroom**: `scale[c]
= global_amax(channel c) * world_size / 127`. The headroom guarantees
every rank's quantized values stay within `[-127/ws, 127/ws]`, so the
element-wise sum over `ws` ranks can **never overflow int8** — this
matters because HCCL int8 reduce wraps modulo 256 instead of saturating
(verified experimentally on 910B3).
2. Tiny fp32 per-channel amax sync (hidden-size elements, a few KB)
before the payload all-reduce.
3. int8 all-reduce (half payload) + dequantization back to bf16.

The per-channel scale is critical for accuracy: a per-tensor scale loses
~2 bits to the headroom and caused measurable accuracy regression on
long-CoT tasks, while the per-channel scheme keeps it within noise.

## Results (4x Atlas 910B3, TP=4, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 16k-token prefill
batches)

| Metric | bf16 baseline | quantized AR |
|---|---|---|
| per-AR latency (64 MiB) | 1.9 ms | 1.4 ms |
| Mean TTFT (vllm bench serve, 16k in / 64 out, 32 prompts @ 2 qps) |
1971 ms | **1473 ms (-25%)** |
| Throughput | 1.54 req/s | **1.61 req/s (+4.5%)** |
| GPQA-diamond (AISBench, 0-shot CoT) | 69.7% | **70.7% (within noise,
z=0.23)** |
| Output degeneration (unparseable / truncated @8k) | 30 / 45 | 29 / 45
(unchanged) |

## Usage

```bash
export VLLM_ASCEND_QUANTIZED_ALL_REDUCE=1
# optional: tune the activation threshold (numel, default 4 MiB of bf16)
export VLLM_ASCEND_QUANTIZED_ALL_REDUCE_MIN_NUMEL=4194304
```

Messages below the threshold stay on the bf16 path (they are
latency-bound; the scale sync would cost more than the halved transfer
saves).

## Test plan

- [x] New UT:
`tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators/test_quantized_all_reduce.py`
(mocked, thresholding + int8 payload path)
- [x] 4-rank microbenchmark: mathematical correctness of the headroom
scheme vs plain int8 wrap on real HCCL
- [x] e2e serving benchmark (vllm bench serve) and GPQA accuracy run on
4x 910B3
- [x] CI

[BugFix][KV Cache] Honor upstream prefix cache retention configuration (#21229)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Ascend hybrid HBM coordinator and AscendStore scheduler/worker still
read
`getattr(vllm.envs, "VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL", None)`.
Upstream vLLM
removed that environment variable in
[vllm#55353](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55353),
so these paths silently select `None` (dense retention) even when the
CLI selects
`0` or a positive interval.

Read `KVCacheConfig.prefix_cache_retention_interval` in the HBM
coordinator and
`VllmConfig.cache_config.prefix_cache_retention_interval` in
AscendStore. Reuse the
existing retention algorithms and validation. Migrate the stale
environment
variable in 12 E2E YAML files to the CLI option on the same instances,
and document
the configuration and upgrade behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The three affected paths now honor the upstream configuration:

| CLI setting | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omitted | `None` (dense) | Upstream default `0` |
| `0` | `None` (dense) | `0` |
| Positive interval | `None` (dense) | Configured interval |
| `None` | `None` (dense) | `None` (dense) |

For sliding-window/Mamba groups, `0` retains the checkpoints needed for
prompt
replay, positive values additionally retain periodic checkpoints, and
`None`
retains reachable checkpoints densely. Full-attention groups retain
their dense
behavior. To preserve the previous effective behavior, explicitly pass
`--prefix-cache-retention-interval None`.

The migrated E2E cases explicitly select `4096`, restoring their
configured intent;
this changes their effective behavior from the previous silent `None`
fallback.
A release note fragment accompanies the configuration fix.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Existing tests:** 384 passed, 12 skipped, and 214 subtests passed
across
seven existing test files against each of vLLM `v0.32.0` and the
CI-pinned
main commit
[`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58).

- **Existing fixture migration:** explicitly select `None` in the shared
scheduler/worker mocks and the two lifecycle cases that assert dense
prefix
hits. All assertions are preserved and no new test cases are added. All
84
tests that failed in the previous CI run pass locally against both
versions.
- **Local test setup:** isolated CPU tests reuse the repository's NPU
stubs,
real upstream cache implementations, and the relevant Ascend
cache/config
patches. Unrelated worker/platform patches are not loaded. Standard

workflow lint, and structural checks. The full command did not pass
